scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Manual-read route completion for 9200 accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026.

F-02.statement: The billing-db tariff change log contains 0 records.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type (billing-db): 1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query identified 14 distinct lagging routes with distinct completion values, e.g. route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: 320 accounts across 40 distinct routes were marked ESTIMATED in the last billing cycle (billing-db).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-AUTOFIX.statement: Dispute volume doubled because ticket response is too slow/manual and because underlying wrong bills can be auto-corrected by an AI agent.

H-RULE-CHANGE-MISBILLING.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August altered estimate-substitution logic, systematically producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-DEGRADED.statement: The nightly MDMS-to-billing export of AMI register reads degraded or failed starting around August, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADED.statement: The manual meter-read handoff from MeterWorks degraded (missed routes or invalid reads) around August, increasing estimate substitutions and bill errors.

H-TICKET-INTAKE-SHIFT.statement: The apparent dispute surge reflects a change in CRM ticket intake or categorization (not an increase in actual billing errors) since August.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) involve ACTUAL, non-estimated reads, suggesting a billing calculation or import defect affecting actual-read bills is a major driver of the dispute surge, distinct from estimate-substitution mechanisms.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-completion log shows manual meter-read routes covering 9200 accounts completed at 88% against a 95% target during Aug-Sep 2026, the same window as the dispute surge, indicating a shortfall of completed manual reads that would force estimate substitutions for the uncompleted accounts.

The billing-db tariff change log contains zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes occurred that could explain the wrong bills behind the dispute surge; this rules out tariff changes as a cause but says nothing about import validation rules, AMI exports, or field reads.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) involved ESTIMATED reads and 1785 (59%) involved ACTUAL reads, so a majority of disputed bills are tied to actual (non-estimated) meter reads rather than estimate substitutions.

CRM dispute-ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026: 610, 590) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), roughly doubling across the Aug-Sep window, confirming the magnitude of the surge in raw ticket counts rather than its cause.

The CRM response-time record for 2440 dispute tickets shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA, indicating response speed is not currently a bottleneck despite the ticket-volume surge.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead), a non-authoritative stakeholder source, states there has been no tariff change this year, which agrees with the authoritative billing-db tariff change log (E-02, 0 records) already used to rule out tariff changes as a cause of the dispute surge. This is corroborating testimony, not new evidence, and does not speak to import validation rules, AMI exports, or field reads.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims a shortage of three readers since July is causing late routes, which forces estimated bills for the affected customers. This is an unverified, non-authoritative stakeholder claim from a source with a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (§4.2) establishes that the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD); this is a document grounding the existing human-approval requirement on push_route_update, not new information about the billing dispute surge's cause.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query returned 14 routes with per-route completion figures (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), operationalizing W-WI-ROUTE-INVESTIGATE by identifying which specific manual-read routes are behind schedule within the aggregate 88% completion shortfall already recorded in E-01.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db reports 320 accounts across 40 distinct routes were marked ESTIMATED in the last billing cycle. This is raw account/route-level data for the estimated-read population, not yet cross-matched against the specific 14 lagging routes (E-09), but the route count (40) already far exceeds the lagging-route count (14).

U-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL-CORRELA.question: Does the manual-read route completion shortfall (88% vs 95%, E-01) actually correlate with the ESTIMATED-read minority (1240 of 3025) of disputes, or is SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-07) overstated given a disclosed incentive bias?

U-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL-CORRELA.resolution_path: Join DA-ROUTE route-completion records with DA-TICKET ESTIMATED-read disputes by account and period.
U-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL-CORRELA.safe_placeholder: Treat the route-completion shortfall as a secondary, unconfirmed contributor; do not push route changes based on it alone.
U-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL-CORRELA.resolution: Estimated accounts cover 40 distinct routes while only 14 routes are flagged as lagging (E-09); this partial mismatch suggests the route-completion shortfall explains only a subset of estimated-read accounts, weakening a full correlation but not yet ruling it out pending route-level matching.

structural_remedies.description: Run a deterministic, read-only query of the DA-RULES billing import validation rule change log (billing-config) for changes coinciding with the August surge start, to test H-RULE-CHANGE-MISBILLING directly.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is already in intended_scope (investigate_billing_import_validation_rules), is read-only (no K-BILLWRITE/K-DISPATCH approval needed), and billing-config is a listed authoritative tool, though its tool_health is currently UNKNOWN and must be checked first.; residual gap: Finding a rule change does not by itself prove causation of the actual-read defect; it must still be timing-correlated with disputed ACTUAL-read bills (DA-BILL) to isolate the mechanism, and tool_health UNKNOWN for billing-config could block the query.

structural_remedies.description: Query DA-BILL for the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills to look for a common calculation pattern (e.g., specific meter class, date range, or import batch) that would pinpoint the defect without needing AMI data.
structural_remedies.rationale: billing-db is HEALTHY and read-only; already within intended_scope (investigate_disputed_actual_read_bills); no approval constraint applies to a read query.; residual gap: DA-BILL completeness is UNKNOWN and the 3025-bill sample's representativeness is itself an open assumption (A-DISPUTED-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATI), so a pattern found here may not generalize, and ambiguous/non-obvious patterns may still require interpretive judgment.
